correctness.rationale: Fallback datum independently replayed from stored adjacency lists with stdlib toolkit: J7 (28v,42e) and J9 (36v,54e) are cubic, simple, bridgeless (lowlink 0 bridges), girth 6 (toolkit BFS and independent brute-force BFS both 6). 3-edge-colour UNSAT via exhaustive perfect-matching enumeration (J7 npm=128, J9 npm=512, limits far below 200k cap) so both are snarks. pi=4 exactly: uncolourability gives pi>=4; branch-and-bound set-cover finds explicit 4-PM covers of all edges (verified union==full), so pi<=4. K26 cross-check also re-verified (npm=40, 4-cover UNSAT, 5-cover SAT, girth 5). Cyclic>=5 exhaustively re-verified: J7 42+861+11480+111930 subsets sizes 1-4 all negative (1.5s); J9 54+1431+24804+316251 subsets sizes 1-4 all negative (sizes 1-3 in 0.4s, size-4 full scan 316251 subsets in 4.5s, found None). Cut predicate (DSU components + m>=n per connected component) is correct definition of cycle-separating. Flow bound verified: stored (9,2)-flows match graph edge-sets exactly, values in [2,7]=[q,p-q], Kirchhoff 0 mod 9 at every vertex via independent verifier (True ok for both). Modular (p,q)=circular p/q equivalence (Goddyn-Tarsi-Zhang) correctly invoked as upper bound only; exact Phi not claimed. Limits honestly stated (headline pi>=5 separator OPEN, lower-ratio searches non-theorems). No essential inference or boundary error in the fallback theorem (a)-(e).

originality.rationale: The fallback joint datum (J7/J9: pi=4, Phi_c<=9/2=4.5, cyclic>=5, girth 6) is not new; both numerical components are substantively recorded or mechanically implied by prior theorems, not merely by failed search. (1) Flow: Goedgebeur-Mattiolo-Mazzuoccolo arXiv:1909.09870 Sec.3 Table 2 reports the Lukotka-Skoviera theorem that Flower snark J_{2k+1} of order 8k+4 has Phi_c=4+1/k. For J7 (28v, 2k+1=7,k=3) this is 4+1/3~=4.333; for J9 (36v,k=4) this is 4+1/4=4.25. Both are strictly stronger than the claimed 4.5 upper bound, which is therefore a weaker corollary, not a new extremal value. An explicit (9,2)-flow is a new certificate for a weaker ratio, not a new mathematical fact. The admission gap analysis omits this source entirely. (2) Covering index: Macajova-Skoviera arXiv:2008.01398 Sec.1 states the Brinkmann et al. exhaustive census of all 64,326,024 cyclically-4-connected girth>=5 snarks to 36 vertices contains only two graphs with pi>=5 (Petersen and one 34-vertex graph). J7 (28v) and J9 (36v) are members of that census class (cyclic>=5 implies cyclic>=4, girth 6, snark), so pi(J7)<=4 and pi(J9)<=4 follow by subtraction; with classical uncolourability (Isaacs) pi=4 follows. Hence pi=4 is census-implied, not a new table entry. Searches for 'perfect matching index flower' returning zero do not establish priority; the census counting theorem is the substantive nearest prior. The strengthened-stratum separator (cyclic-5,girth>=6,pi>=5,Phi<5) itself remains open and is correctly not claimed, so no originality credit attaches to the missed headline.

value.rationale: Judging the strongest self-contained fallback claim (J7/J9 cyclic-5 girth-6 snarks with pi=4 and Phi<=4.5 plus family pi table) on its own: it is a correct re-certification of classic objects (Isaacs Flower snarks, 1975) at values already known or implied in stronger form. Per the narrow-datum standard, an exact invariant of a natural motivated object is retrievable only when the value is not known or mechanically implied and a future researcher could need the precise fact. Here Phi<=4.5 is implied by the known exact 4+1/3 and 4+1/4 values, and pi=4 is implied by the published to-36-vertex pi>=5 census; the new work weakens the flow optimum and re-derives the covering number by enumeration. Certification alone (explicit (9,2)-flows, PM covers, cut logs) does not rescue a weaker restatement of known numbers, and the incomplete survey around it is honestly described as non-theorem but adds no independent theorem, criterion, or downstream use beyond reusable adjacency lists for already-tabled invariants. This is a textbook-parameter re-verification / weaker-bound substitution, not an independently worth-finding-later datum.

decisive_checks: Replayed J7/J9 cubic+simple+bridgeless+girth-6 (toolkit girth + independent BFS brute force both 6) and edge-set match of flow files (42/54 edges).
Replayed snark status: is_3_edge_colourable exhaustive over enumerated PMs gives J7 npm=128 UNSAT, J9 npm=512 UNSAT.
Replayed pi=4: min_cover_depth finds 4-PM cover with union==full for J7 and J9; uncolourability blocks 3.
Replayed Phi<=9/2: verify_circular_flow with identity orientation gives True ok for both; values min 2 max 7 within [2,7].

Re-ran full cyclic>=5 scans: J7 42/861/11480/111930 all negative; J9 54/1431/24804/316251 all negative (size-4 316251 subsets, 4.5s, None). Random connected-subset search finds min cycle-separating boundary 6, consistent with >=5.
Re-verified K26 (26v) girth 5, bridgeless, 3-col UNSAT npm=40, 4-cover UNSAT, 5-cover SAT covering all.

Substantive priority comparison: computed 4+1/3=4.333 and 4+1/4=4.25 from Table-2 formula vs claimed 4.5 (strictly weaker); mapped J7/J9 orders 28=8*3+4, 36=8*4+4 to k=3,4; applied 64M-graph to-36v only-two-pi>=5 census to J7/J9 membership to derive pi=4 by subtraction.
residual_risks: PM-enumeration and 3-colour/set-cover code assumed exhaustive; risk mitigated by far-below-limit npm counts, matching published npm magnitudes, and independent K26/J7/J9 re-runs, but no second independent PM enumerator was written.

Cyclic-scan predicate audited by inspection (m>=n per DSU component) and by random-search sanity (min separating boundary 6); a subtle non-induced-cut encoding bug would affect both candidate and verifier identically, but full-combination counts match C(m,k) and timing scales as expected.
Modular-to-circular flow equivalence relied on cited Goddyn-Tarsi-Zhang theorem without re-proof; standard and correctly applied as upper bound only.

Originality rests on published Table-2 exact Flower flow formula and published census counting statement; full-text verification of Lukotka-Skoviera 2008 proof was via the secondary Table-2 citation plus abstract, not line-by-line re-derivation, but the numerical implication (4.33/4.25 < 4.5) is unambiguous.
